statement: The product $1 \times 2 \times 3 \times \cdots \times 40$ is written out in full as an ordinary whole number. How many zeros are at the end of this number?

choices.misconception: I only counted the multiples of $10$, which are $10, 20, 30, 40$, so I got $4$ zeros.
I counted one factor of $5$ for each multiple of $5$ up to $40$, but forgot that $25 = 5 \cdot 5$ gives an extra $5$.
I counted one zero for each of the $8$ multiples of $5$ and another zero for each of the $4$ multiples of $10$, counting those $5$s twice.
I counted the factors of $2$ in the product, $20 + 10 + 5 + 2 + 1 = 38$, instead of the factors of $5$.

hints: Each zero at the end comes from a factor of $10 = 2 \cdot 5$.
There are far more factors of $2$ than of $5$, so count the factors of $5$ in the product.
The multiples of $5$ up to $40$ are $5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40$, and $25$ contains $5$ twice.

solutions.reliable: Each trailing zero needs one factor of $2$ and one factor of $5$. Factors of $2$ are plentiful, so the count is set by the factors of $5$. The multiples of $5$ from $1$ to $40$ are $5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40$; each gives one $5$, and $25 = 5^2$ gives one extra. That is $8 + 1 = 9$ factors of $5$, so the number ends in $9$ zeros.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
